texto: Existential pain is the rent existence charges, and no one lives here free Existential suffering is not cured by metaphysical tricks. Whether one calls the system “John” or strips away the name, the structure still generates the same anxiety, dread, and bodily unrest. Pain arises from the organism’s core function: processing risk, finitude, and the certainty of death. No identity label softens that load. This is why “you are not John” narratives can be not just hollow but cruel, suggesting a loophole where none exists. The only pragmatic gain in stepping back from identity is sharper perception. You gain cleaner feedback loops, less distortion but this does not dissolve the existential weight. Suffering is built-in, a structural tax for being an organism that knows it exists. The fact of it is indifferent to metaphysical reframing; it is as raw and inescapable as the conditions of life itself.
